jobs.title: EI&O Workplace Technology Program Manager
jobs.location: 100 New Millennium Way, Bldg 2, Durham NC
jobs.description:
Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

Job Description:

The Role

Are you energized by leading large-scale technology programs that transform the workplace experience? As an EI&O Workplace Technology Program Manager, you will play a critical leadership role in delivering complex, cross-functional initiatives that enable Fidelity's evolving workplace strategy. Working closely with Real Estate, Architecture & Engineering, Enterprise Infrastructure, End User Computing, Security, Product Management, and external partners, you will drive the planning, coordination, and execution of technology programs supporting modernization efforts.

The Expertise and Skills You Bring

This role is responsible for leading multiple concurrent programs that span network infrastructure, wireless, telecommunications, audiovisual systems, workplace technology platforms, and end-user technology services. You will bring together diverse stakeholders, manage competing priorities, mitigate risks, and ensure successful delivery of business-critical initiatives while aligning with enterprise technology standards, operational requirements, and long-term workplace technology strategies.

Key capabilities include:
- 10+ years experience leading and managing large-scale office renovations and campus builds, with a focus on technology rooms, structured cabling, wireless, audio-visual, smart building and end user technologies.

- Demonstrated track record of successfully delivering cross-functional initiatives involving multiple business and technology teams, vendors, and executive stakeholders.

- Strong leadership and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority and drive alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.

- Deep knowledge of program management frameworks, tools, and methodologies, including Agile, Waterfall, hybrid delivery approaches, risk management, and governance practices.

- Proven ability to develop and manage program roadmaps, integrated project plans, budgets, dependencies, schedules, risks, issues, and resource requirements across multiple concurrent initiatives.

- Experience partnering with real estate, construction, architecture, and engineering teams to coordinate technology delivery within office build, renovation, or relocation programs.

- Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and make informed, data-driven decisions.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop executive-level communications, facilitate steering committees, and present program status, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership.

- Ability to establish governance, drive accountability, and coordinate successful program execution while balancing immediate business requirements with long-term strategic objectives.

- Experience managing external vendors, consultants, and service providers to ensure successful delivery, quality outcomes, and adherence to enterprise standards.

- Knowledge of workplace technology trends and emerging technologies, with the ability to evaluate solutions that support scalable, flexible, and future-ready workplace environments.

The Team

The EI&O Workplace Technology team is responsible for delivering infrastructure and technology solutions that enable our offices to operate effectively and scale for the future.

We partner closely with real estate, construction, engineering, and technology teams to deliver secure, reliable, future-ready infrastructure that supports an excellent associate experience in every location.

Fidelity manages more than 11 million square feet of space in the United States and overseas, including thirteen North American and six international locations, two data centers and more than 200 retail investor centers.

Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

jobs.title: International Small Cap Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Note: Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for U.S.-based employment associated with this position.

The Role
The International Small Cap Research Analyst will work closely with Fidelity's portfolio managers and play a vital role in contributing to our mutual funds’ investment performance. The analyst will be responsible for researching and covering companies within designated sectors of the international small cap universe and developing investment recommendations through deep fundamental analysis.

Analysts have full responsibility for coverage of assigned companies.  This includes building financial models, analyzing industry dynamics, assessing valuation opportunities, conducting proprietary research, meeting with company management teams and communicating investment recommendations.

The Value You Deliver
You will identify new investment opportunities and monitor existing positions across your assigned sectors. Working closely with portfolio managers and fellow analysts, you will contribute to portfolio performance through high-conviction investment ideas based on independent thinking and differentiated research.

Responsibilities include:
- Generating investment ideas through proprietary research, quantitative screens, company meetings, industry conferences, and other research sources. Performing fundamental company, industry, and competitive analysis.

- Identifying underfollowed, misunderstood, or mispriced companies before they become broadly recognized by the market. Creating and maintaining financial models, valuations, recommendations, and target prices.

- Communicating investment insights and recommendations with conviction and clarity through discussions, presentations, and written research.

- Collaborating with analysts and portfolio managers in a high-performing, results-oriented investment environment.

The Expertise and Skills You Bring
- Multiple years of investment research experience, preferably in international equities, global equities, or small-cap investing.

- Bachelor's degree required; CFA or advanced degree preferred.

- Demonstrated passion for investing, stock picking, and fundamental research. Strong ownership mentality, work ethic, and commitment to investment excellence.

- Exceptional analytical, financial modeling, and communication skills. Ability to think independently and adapt as new information emerges.

- Strong business judgment, intellectual curiosity, and pattern recognition abilities.

- Confidence and maturity to engage with senior management teams.

The Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a passionate investor who thrives on uncovering underfollowed companies, developing differentiated perspectives, and generating ideas that positively impact portfolio performance. They combine rigorous analytical skills with intellectual curiosity, and independent thinking.

Most importantly, they are motivated by the pursuit of investment excellence and a desire to deliver strong outcomes for clients.

The Group
Fidelity Investments has long been a leader in managing equity portfolios, with roots dating back to the 1940s. Fidelity’s Equity division is responsible for managing diversified and industry-specific funds for millions of investors. The division consists of portfolio managers, research analysts, research associates, sector specialists, and traders who work together to deliver exceptional investment outcomes. Over the years, its capabilities have grown substantially, with investment strategies designed across style, capitalization, sector, and geography.

The Equity team relies on its proprietary research, disciplined portfolio management, and sophisticated trading process to evaluate, construct, and manage investment portfolios and deliver superior long-term results.

Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model
Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

The base salary range for this position is $150,000 - $250,000 per year.   Placement in the range will vary based on job responsibilities and scope, geographic location, candidate’s relevant experience, and other factors.

Base salary is only part of the total compensation package. Depending on the position and eligibility requirements, the offer package may also include bonus or other variable compensation.

We offer a wide range of benefits to meet your evolving needs and help you live your best life at work and at home.  These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage and emotional well-being support, market-leading retirement, generous paid time off and parental leave, charitable giving employee match program, and educational assistance including student loan repayment, tuition reimbursement, and learning resources to develop your career.  Note, the application window closes when the position is filled or unposted.

Job Description:

The Role
Equity Research Analyst summer interns work closely with Fidelity's Portfolio Managers and play a vital role in contributing to the investment performance of the firm. Interns take ownership of fundamental equity research coverage for a group of companies within a designated industry.
Responsibilities includes conducting in-depth company and industry analysis, engaging with management teams and industry experts, evaluating customers, suppliers, and competitors, building detailed financial models, and synthesizing company, industry, and macroeconomic insights into actionable investment recommendations.
Throughout the internship, each intern develops and articulate investment theses on their assigned companies and presents investment recommendations to Fidelity Analysts, Portfolio Managers, and senior leaders. Interns receive mentorship, coaching, and ongoing feedback from an experienced member of Fidelity's Equity Research team while building relationships across the organization and gaining exposure to Fidelity's investment process.
